findings_and_questions.observation: The assigned helper filters the incoming CharacterView.alive value and clones retained views; it has no database read, timing check, completeness witness, permission decision or actual-life guarantee. Upstream omits unavailable and ahead-of-observer rows, projects death at observer time and may intentionally conceal uncertain or future death. Native living IDs derive from stored actual Character.alive, and native require_party_ready explicitly rejects an empty actual living set.
findings_and_questions.qualification: Distinguish observer-time presentation from authoritative life; the source does not prove resurrection, disclosure, unauthorized action or an invalid direct use. ROOT-CAMERA-NATIVE2-ADM03-342 and q2452 are historical related scoped dispositions, not a new issue count.
findings_and_questions.future_repair_direction: Only if later authorization and policy analysis require it, keep complete/unavailable and observed/actual life provenance explicit through the owning presentation-to-action boundary while preserving future-death nondisclosure and native authority.

findings_and_questions.kind: historical observation reconnected, no automatic new count
findings_and_questions.observation: An empty or partial visible roster can result from defaulted failed lookups or visibility filtering. Helper’s empty result feeds rest defaults and forecast consumers; with other catalogue/query checks passing, provisioning constructs a Some forecast reporting zero living_members. The quest readiness helper independently filters the original observed roster by participates_in_party_readiness and its initial true survives an empty loop. This latter readiness calculation does not call living_party_members; only the upstream roster is shared.
findings_and_questions.qualification: Historical 774 ADM03-342 already observed empty readiness fold; q1869 and q1871 retain separate readiness and provision questions. No actual failure, empty live party, forecast arithmetic, actor action, rendered control or server acceptance observed. Legitimate empty/absent and privacy-hidden states must not be blanket failures; central decides first-cause aliases.
findings_and_questions.future_repair_direction: Consider representing observation completeness before numerical preview/readiness claims and preserve both intended empty/no-party states and native actual-living enforcement; compare actual consumers before any repair.

findings_and_questions.kind: newly assessed conditional subject/feedback policy question; unique count and canonical owner centrally pending
findings_and_questions.observation: Service role preview collects capabilities for all membership IDs and reports the best individual, with no living or frontier filter in that collection; the sender posts only the selected character. Native request requires that actor to be its current party leader and computes the stored meets_requirements from that actor’s freshly refreshed capability; the receiving panel displays that actor and the stored individual result. If another member meets every recommendation but the leader does not and other conditions pass, party-best preview and leader-only request can convey different assessments about different subjects. A retained deceased member’s capability can enter preview if such a membership and row remain; ordinary reachability is not established.
findings_and_questions.qualification: Both statements may be literally true: one describes a party member and one the named applicant. Need product policy on whose suitability is promised, supported merge/recruitment flow and subject identity. No actual request, stale data, misleading UI, unauthorized join, or independent accepted defect is established. Do not equate this with q191 capability-availability or q179 observer-frontier first cuts merely because both touch this code.
findings_and_questions.future_repair_direction: After central reconciliation and separate implementation authorization, if consistency is required, make the preview subject and submitted recipient explicit or use a shared chosen-subject assessment while preserving party-versus-individual recommendations and native authorization.

findings_and_questions.kind: connected existing policy/failure families; no assumed aliases
findings_and_questions.observation: Preview ignores the capability refresh result, then queries the capability row: if refresh fails and a prior row remains, the match can use it; absent/error query produces no candidate. Raw membership/capability preview does not use the visibility-filtered observed roster, so a future-ahead member’s state could affect the match if query permissions and chronology permit. Native request refreshes the actor separately and propagates failure before insertion.
findings_and_questions.qualification: q191 concerns projection availability; q179 concerns observer frontier/snapshot. Their exact alias relationship to these distinct service first sites is unresolved. No stale row, query failure, actual future-data disclosure, recipient outcome or browser result is claimed.
findings_and_questions.future_repair_direction: If later evidence establishes an unacceptable result, retain refresh and observation availability through the preview and apply the agreed observer/snapshot policy; preserve recipient authority and legitimate valid empty data.

open_questions: Does product policy intentionally compare the entire source party in the sender preview while recording only the leader on the target-side request? Which subject should be presented and why?
Can a dead or observer-ahead member retain an accessible capability row during supported recruitment, and what observation policy applies to current capability summaries?
When roster fetch/visibility gives no rows, should forecast readiness be unavailable, no-party, or another explicit state? Can a normal valid party reach the condition?

Do actual consumers distinguish the zero-member forecast from a complete calculation, and which action reducer imposes its independent actual-life check? No assumption every action calls the inspected native readiness gate.
What consistency and freshness guarantees exist across separate membership, capability, character-time and condition reads? Actual database snapshot/custody behavior was not probed.
All other original roles, other lens populations, actual native UI behavior and product acceptance remain centrally unresolved.

thirteen_lenses.producer-propagation: CharacterView projected alive feeds helper, forecast IDs and separate readiness predicate; service recruitment bypasses that helper and builds a separate raw capability set. Trace observed vs native authority and candidate identity explicitly.
thirteen_lenses.existing-type-owners: CharacterView, CharacterCapability, CharacterCapabilities, native RoleRequirements and request fields have distinct current purposes; matching bytes or bool fields do not prove a complete roster or one same-subject owner.
thirteen_lenses.admission-contracts: Helper filters a supplied projection, not authorization. Native require_party_ready and join request have separate actual life/actor checks. Empty roster and failed refresh remain conditional availability questions.
thirteen_lenses.invariant-operations: Clone/filter preserve input order and do not mutate alive state; a max over zero capabilities and an all-fold over zero observed members have different source semantics. No phantom arithmetic or fabricated transaction.
thirteen_lenses.aggregate-states: Retained membership, observer time, character life, capability freshness, role requirements and leader identity need correlated evidence. Party-best and submitted individual may legitimately differ pending UX policy.
thirteen_lenses.type-ownership: Observer-time projection is web-owned, actual living membership and join authority native-owned; do not authorize gameplay from a display filter or turn intentional future concealment into truth about current life.
thirteen_lenses.redundant-authority: Quest readiness filters alive separately, and service match uses raw membership; these are different derived use sites, not independently proved duplicate authority or mandatory dedup.
thirteen_lenses.behavior-preservation: Keep corpses visible where intended but out of survivor readiness; preserve concealment of future deaths, valid empty/optional data, leader authorization, accepted native request modes and no compatibility fallback.
thirteen_lenses.enum-shapes: A bool alive within an observed view cannot itself describe unavailable, observer-hidden or actual-current status; whether explicit state is needed belongs to the upstream owner/policy. No mandatory enum established for seven-line helper alone.
thirteen_lenses.derivability: Iterator filter/clone/collect is direct; no handwritten trait or serialization defect established in the assigned helper. q2452 scoped DTO nonfinding remains attributed to historical root.
thirteen_lenses.granularity: Separate projected alive, actual living, entire party potential, individual leader eligibility and error/valid absence. Do not conflate them because fields share bool or IDs.
thirteen_lenses.magic-strings: The seven-line helper has no string; raw service match levels and labels are presentation values, native SQL and fixed reducer names are boundary strings. No whole string-family verdict or invalid prose classifier alleged.
thirteen_lenses.magic-numbers: The assigned filter has no raw numeric literal. Other source counts/ratings belong to their own producer and native role policy, not a blanket magic-number finding. Fatigue and encumbrance must respect root combat legibility rules.
